To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the volume dependence in the spectral weight function can be expressed in terms of a generalized formula which includes both single-particle and multi-particle cases, and the volume dependence of spectral weights of a narrow resonance and a broad resonance are different.

we have found a generalized formula for the spectral weight functions which incorporates both narrow resonance and broad resonance cases, and that the spectral weight functions exhibit single-particle behavior in the extreme narrow resonance region, two-particle behavior in a broad resonance region, and an intermediate behavior in a resonance region.

we have derived a general formula for the spectral weight functions of both $A_1^+$ and $T^-_{1}$ channels which incorporates both narrow resonance and broad resonance cases and the volume dependence of spectral weights for narrow resonance is the same as that of the two-particle scattering states while for broad resonance, the volume dependence of a broad resonance shares that of a two-particles scattering state.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the volume dependence of spectral functions and the corresponding two-point functions for both $A_1^+$ and $T_1^-$ channels, which are crucial for the extraction of resonance masses and decay constants from lattice QCD calculations.
the study of volume dependence of the two-point correlation functions for the $\eta$ and $\eta'$ mesons in the $T^-_0$ and $T^+_0$ channels.
the volume dependence of spectral weights in lattice QCD and the corresponding implications on the extraction of resonance properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the volume dependence is determined by the width of the resonance.
the volume dependence is a good tool for distinguishing a single-particle from a two-particle state.
the spectral weight functions are proportional to $1/V$ in the limit of $V \rightarrow \infty$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spectral weight functions for a narrow and broad resonance are quite similar to the two-particle case and the single-particle case respectively.

the spectral weight formula derived in the present study can be used to distinguish the single-particle from the two-particle states in lattice QCD simulations and it can also be used to determine the mass and width of a resonance in a large cubic finite-volume lattice calculation.
the spectral weight functions for narrow and broad resonances can be distinguished in a finite volume.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the volume dependence can be used to distinguish between single- and multi-particle states, even for a broad resonance.
the volume dependence is an important indicator of the underlying physical nature of the state in question and it should be taken into account in the extraction of the resonance parameters.
, for a narrow resonance, its spectral weight function can be used to distinguish it from the multi-particle scattering state.
